correctness.rationale: The exact coefficient-level product identity gives E²=U for invertible A_H. Propagating a squared generator across connected edges forces every nonzero ideal to contain U; any superspace of U is an ideal. Independence of the squared vectors makes zero products equivalent to per-fibre Euclidean orthogonality, forcing any ambient natural basis to consist of fibre-supported vectors. Orthogonal complements characterize all ideals admitting an extendible natural basis. For d-regular H, the Kronecker spectrum and classical Cheeger inequalities yield h(G)>=b h(H)^2/(4d). Finite direct-definition tests, natural-basis exhaustive checks over F3, orthogonal basis tests, and small cut censuses succeeded; no finite test is treated as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Exact opposed ideal lattices in a natural infinite graph-algebra family reveal an algebraic structure invisible to ordinary connectivity and uniform Cheeger expansion. For double blowups the extension-property ideal lattice is Boolean with 2^n+1 elements including zero, whereas the real ordinary ideal lattice contains a continuum. A spectrally uniform family thereby exposes a substantive boundary of a specifically published 2026 simplicity assertion. The result is not merely a tiny finite counterexample or a restatement of earlier general non-simplicity criteria.
